entities.name: Matteo II Visconti
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Matteo II Visconti, who died on October 7, 1355, was one of three co-rulers of Milan, sharing the lordship with his brothers Galeazzo II and Bernabò Visconti. Born into the powerful Visconti dynasty, which had consolidated its control over Milan and much of Lombardy, Matteo's brief period of rule from 1349 was marked by internal family dynamics and the ongoing expansionist ambitions of the Milanese state. His inheritance, following the death of his uncle Archbishop Giovanni Visconti, placed him in a unique, albeit precarious, position within one of Italy's most formidable medieval city-states, at a time when Northern Italy was a crucible of political innovation and ruthless dynastic struggles.

Upon the death of Archbishop Giovanni Visconti in 1354, the vast Visconti dominion was formally partitioned among his three nephews, as per his will. Matteo II was assigned territories including Bologna, Lodi, Parma, and Piacenza, while Galeazzo II received Pavia and Como, and Bernabò took Bergamo, Cremona, and Brescia, with Milan itself divided among them. Matteo's rule was characterized by a perceived indolence and a penchant for cruelty, which reportedly alienated both his subjects and his own family. His administration of Bologna, a strategically vital Papal city often contested by Milan, was particularly turbulent, drawing the ire of Pope Innocent VI and contributing to the volatile political landscape of the Romagna.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Matteo II Visconti's brief and tumultuous co-rulership, ending in his suspicious death, was a pivotal moment for the Visconti dynasty, directly leading to the consolidation of power by his brothers Galeazzo II and Bernabò and shaping the future of Milanese expansion.
